en.title: Workplace Harassment: What Evidence Should You Keep?
en.directAnswer: If workplace conduct is harming or threatening you, protect your safety first. Keep a private factual record of dates, messages, emails, witnesses and reports made to HR or management. The correct legal route depends on the conduct. Some cases may involve labour law, workplace policy, civil rights or criminal offences.

en.lawMeaning: This page should focus on evidence and safe reporting, not make a legal finding from one short description. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Use internal complaint route when safe.
Use police/legal help if there are threats, assault or other offences.
evidence: Messages; email; incident log; witness list; HR complaint; medical record; employment documents.
en.simpleExample: An employee reports repeated threatening messages from a supervisor. Saving the original messages and a dated HR complaint is stronger than only telling colleagues verbally.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: posting private company data online.
Common mistakes: confronting a dangerous person alone.
Common mistakes: deleting messages after screenshotting only part of the conversation..

whatIf.question: What if HR is the problem?
whatIf.answer: Use an independent senior/authority route where available.

whatIf.question: What if there is physical danger?
whatIf.answer: Safety and emergency reporting come first.

whatIf.question: What if you fear retaliation?
whatIf.answer: Keep copies of lawful evidence outside the work device.

en.specialistTrigger: Threats; sexual violence; assault; blackmail; retaliation; termination after complaint.
